vocabulary.meaning: the habit of spending as little money as possible
examples: Penny-pinching can be useful when money is tight.
His extreme penny-pinching annoyed his family.

vocabulary.meaning: careful about spending money and avoiding waste
examples: She is frugal but not unwilling to enjoy life.
A frugal lifestyle can help people save.

vocabulary.meaning: a plan for how money will be earned and spent
examples: We created a monthly household budget.
Sticking to a budget can prevent unnecessary debt.
Housing is our biggest monthly expense.
The company is trying to reduce unnecessary expenses.

vocabulary.meaning: to keep money instead of spending it
examples: They save part of every salary payment.
Small changes can help you save money.

vocabulary.meaning: to reduce the amount of something you use or spend
examples: We cut back on restaurant meals to save money.
The family had to cut back after energy prices increased.

vocabulary.meaning: something sold for a lower price than expected
examples: The second-hand table was a real bargain.
She enjoys looking for bargains at the market.

vocabulary.meaning: a reduction in the normal price
examples: Students receive a ten-percent discount.
The shop offered a large discount during the sale.
Food and housing are essential expenses.
When money is limited, focus on essential purchases.

vocabulary.meaning: to reduce spending and use resources carefully
examples: Many households are trying to economise on energy.
We economised by cooking more meals at home.
